stories.title: AI is changing cancer treatment — and a new breakthrough shows just how far we've come
stories.synopsis: AI is helping researchers rethink cancer treatment, and a new result is encouraging. In a trial, a vaccine combined with the immunotherapy drug Keytruda reduced the relative risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The vaccine is not yet FDA-approved, but the work points toward more personalized cancer care.

stories.title: Google.org awards Clalit $2 million to develop AI system for patient access
stories.synopsis: Google.org has granted Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest healthcare provider, $2 million to build a conversational AI platform. Over two years, the system aims to help about five million members book appointments, complete intake forms, and get follow-up guidance in multiple languages and regional dialects. It also targets patients with limited internet access, so more people can reach care more easily.

stories.title: AI medicine breakthrough: Could 'good viruses' created by AI, cure deadly viruses?
stories.synopsis: Scientists report that AI-designed viruses were used to treat a patient with a life-threatening E. coli infection that had resisted antibiotics and every phage doctors could find. The FDA authorized a trial after the company screened the viruses for safety. The work has not yet been peer-reviewed, and results could take months, but it offers a hopeful new path.
